brief: Create one original, useful article and one Facebook post linking to it about AI concepts, emerging research, enterprise AI engineering use cases, implementation best practices, security, safety, and responsible adoption. Follow the assigned editorial theme and recent-publication exclusions. Be provider-neutral: product announcements are supporting examples, not the default subject. Explain practical tradeoffs, limitations, and actionable lessons. Ground factual claims in retrieved sources; distinguish reported facts from analysis. Never present evergreen guidance as breaking news. Mention Bun2too services only when relevant.
audience: A broad public audience, with an emphasis on technical readers interested in IT, AI, software engineering, and data. Keep explanations accessible to nontechnical readers while providing useful technical detail.
brand_guidelines: Helpful, factual, and educational. Explain technical terms clearly and avoid hype. Distinguish established capabilities, experimental ideas, and predictions. Describe the CrewAI-operated team as a proof of concept; distinguish intended capabilities from demonstrated results. Do not invent news, sources, market statistics, testimonials, prices, offers, or performance results.
business_facts: Bun2too is a software engineering service provider. One example of its products is this proof of concept for a team operated by CrewAI AI agents. The proof of concept illustrates Bun2too's work with software engineering and AI-agent teams.
